name: Congenital Aortic Valve Dysplasia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Echocardiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Aortic Valve Dysplasia

criteria.description: Abnormal aortic valve leaflet morphology including thickening, dysplastic leaflets, or fusion
Evidence of aortic valve dysfunction such as stenosis or regurgitation on echocardiography
Exclusion of other congenital heart defects that could explain valve abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of abnormal valve morphology with associated valve dysfunction on echocardiography
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on echocardiographic findings supported by clinical presentation

pathognomonic.symptomName: Systolic ejection murmur at the right upper sternal border
searchTerms: heart murmur during systole at right upper chest
murmur at right upper sternal border

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital aortic valve leaflet thickening and dysplasia
searchTerms: thickened and malformed aortic valve leaflets
aortic valve dysplasia present at birth

common.symptomName: Exertional dyspnea due to aortic valve stenosis
searchTerms: shortness of breath with exercise from valve narrowing
exertional breathlessness due to aortic stenosis
difficulty breathing on exertion from valve disease

common.symptomName: Fatigue related to decreased cardiac output
searchTerms: fatigue due to low cardiac output
feeling of fast or irregular heartbeats
bounding pulses from leaking aortic valve
strong pulse due to aortic regurgitation
wide pulse pressure from valve leak

occasional.symptomName: Syncope related to severe aortic stenosis
searchTerms: passing out related to heart valve disease

occasional.symptomName: Left ventricular hypertrophy detected on ECG
searchTerms: left ventricular hypertrophy on heart tracing
enlarged left heart muscle detected electrically
getting tired easily with physical activity
infection of heart lining and valves

laboratory: Elevated B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) in advanced valve dysfunction
Normal inflammatory markers unless endocarditis present
imaging: Echocardiography showing dysplastic aortic valve leaflets with stenosis or regurgitation
Cardiac MRI for detailed valve and ventricular assessment
Chest X-ray showing cardiomegaly in advanced disease
genetic: No specific gene identified; possible familial clustering in some cases
other: Electrocardiogram showing left ventricular hypertrophy or arrhythmias

distinguishingFeatures: Typically two leaflets instead of three
Presence of other rheumatic valve lesions

redFlags: Signs of heart failure in infancy or childhood
references: Maron BJ, et al. Congenital heart disease: diagnosis and management. Circulation. 2020.
Nishimura RA, et al. 2020 AHA/ACC Guideline for the Management of Patients With Valvular Heart Disease. Circulation. 2021.
